children.text: Brandon is an operating advisor at Bessemer where he brings a wealth of experience in product leadership, with a particular emphasis in scaling product organizations for growth companies.

Brandon began his product career at Procore Technologies, where he spent 9 years, and he started as the 13th employee and first product manager. He lead product until he left as SVP Product in 2020. During his tenure, the company went from an early-stage startup to a $300M+ in revenue and $5B+ in valuation. He led and oversaw numerous product strategies, including growing from a single-product into a multi-product platform, moving upmarket, launching an open API & developer ecosystem, and launching into several new customer types, verticals, and geographies. Brandon also built and scaled the teams across product management, product design, and product marketing, growing the product team from 1 to north of 100+ at its peak.

Brandon was most recently the senior vice president of product at Shippo, the “shipping layer of the internet”. During his time, Brandon scaled the product team from 5 to 33, and built the product design and product ops & analytics functions from scratch. He also re-envisioned and led a new product strategy to reposition Shippo from being an application company, to a shipping infrastructure/platform company. This led to landing partnerships with Shopify and other major e-commerce players to power their shipping applications.
Brandon holds a Bachelor’s Degree in business economics from UC Santa Barbara, and currently lives in southern California.
Breyton Summer is a senior partnership accountant on the GPA team based out of Bessemer’s Larchmont office.
Previously, Breyton was an audit associate at PwC where he worked with clients in the healthcare industry and gained experience with the IPO process.
Breyton is a CPA and earned his BS and master’s degree in accounting from Binghamton University. In his spare time, he enjoys playing sports and traveling.
Deepa is vice president of talent and community based in Bessemer’s India office.

Prior to joining Bessemer, Deepa was the director of talent acquisition at Unacademy, a multi-lingual edtech company, where she worked closely with the founder on leadership hiring, employer branding, candidate experience, and engagement initiatives. Before joining Unacademcy, Deepa worked at boutique executive talent acquisition and advisory firms including WalkWater Talent Advisors and Longhouse Consulting. There she hired leadership talent for venture capital firms and their portfolio companies across consumer internet and enterprise SaaS startups. Prior to a career move into Executive Search in 2014, Deepa was a corporate sales professional at companies including George P Johnson, an experiential marketing agency, Brand-comm, a PR & brand consulting firm, and Les Concierges, an employee benefits services startup.  During her initial years of career, Deepa also worked as a media planner and buyer at Initiative, an IPG Group company.
Deepa earned her degree in commercial practice from Bangalore University. In her leisure time, she enjoys reading, traveling, and exploring new cuisines.
Darsh is an investor based out of Bessemer’s New York City office. He focuses on enterprise software with a particular interest in infrastructure, cybersecurity, and vertical SaaS.
Prior to joining Bessemer, Darsh worked in operations at Rightway Healthcare and had roles spanning engineering and product management at other early-stage startups.

Darsh graduated from the Johns Hopkins University with general and departmental honors with a B.S. in biomedical engineering and applied mathematics. In his free time, you can find him bouldering, running, rooting for the Yankees, Rangers, and Knicks, or watching Formula 1.

Kayla Gu is a technology executive and go-to-market leader with a track record of building and scaling enterprise businesses through periods of transformational growth. As Vice President of Enterprise Sales at Databricks, she has spent nearly seven years playing a key role in scaling the company's go-to-market organization from its early days to more than $7 billion in annualized revenue today.

During her tenure at Databricks, Kayla has helped build a world-class sales organization and a culture of sales excellence through one of the fastest periods of growth in enterprise software. She has played a key role in evolving the company's GTM model, including its consumption-based sales motion, while building and leading high-performing teams that have delivered consistent growth at scale. Prior to joining Databricks, Kayla held sales leadership roles across both high-growth startups and Oracle Corporation, giving her experience across different stages of company growth and go-to-market maturity.

Kayla partners closely with founders and GTM leaders who are designing and scaling enterprise GTM, building sales motions for consumption-based business models, and moving from founder-led sales to a repeatable sales engine. She also works with teams on segmentation, coverage, and pipeline-generation models; breaking into the Fortune 500 and winning transformational customers; and hiring, developing, and scaling high-performing sales organizations through periods of hypergrowth.

Kayla brings a builder's mindset and a scaled operator's perspective, with firsthand experience navigating the GTM journey from early-stage growth to multi-billion-dollar scale.
Nicolas Salaverria is an accounting manager in the Larchmont office and is responsible for the finance accounting and operations of Bessemer’s US management company and global subsidiaries.

Nicolas earned his bachelor’s degree in accounting from Marist College and his master’s in accounting from Liberty University. Before joining Bessemer, he worked as an audit associate at KPMG, a financial planning analyst at Institutional Investor, and a business transformation manager at CFGI.
Nicolas enjoys traveling, playing golf, dining out, cheering for his favorite sports teams, and spending time with friends and family in his spare time.
Monica Gomez Chico is an office and compliance coordinator based in Bessemer’s Larchmont office.

Prior to joining Bessemer, Monica spent her professional career as a self-employed entrepreneur, launching two businesses. In 2005, she co-founded Gourmetrica, a Mexico City-based company offering team building through cooking activities. In 2019, she launched The Work Inn, a low-cost coworking space in Larchmont. Though it has since closed, it remains one of her most rewarding experiences to date.

Monica received her BA in communications and media studies from the University of Anahuac. She was born and raised in Mexico City and moved to New York, where she currently resides with her husband and two daughters, Fernanda and Emilia. In her free time, Monica enjoys baking, cooking, reading mystery novels, and hiking with her family.

Pete Persampieri is a fund controller on the finance team based in Bessemer’s Larchmont office. In his role, he works on the firm’s financial reporting, investor communications, and portfolio valuations.

Pete began his career at EY providing assurance services on their financial services team. Pete eventually transitioned to EY's advisory group, where he focused on valuation and business modeling services for audit and M&A transactions. Pete joined Bessemer in 2016.
Pete earned his MBA and BS in accounting from Providence College and is a Certified Public Accountant.
Yael Schiff is a vice president in the Israel office, where she focuses primarily on early-stage companies, especially in AI infrastructure, AI applications, cyber, and data.

Prior to Bessemer, Yael was a GM at Via Transportation where her team led partnerships with cities and transit agencies. She was also a consultant at McKinsey and a line planner at Applied Materials earlier in her career.

Yael earned her MBA from Harvard Business School and graduated magna cum laude a B.Sc. in industrial engineering from Tel-Aviv University. In her free time, she enjoys musicals and camping trips with her friends and family.
Grace is an investor with Bessemer’s growth investment practice in San Francisco, where she primarily focuses on AI and software investments.

Prior to joining Bessemer, Grace was an Associate at Centana Growth Partners, where she worked on early-stage growth investments in software and fintech. She was also previously at Oliver Wyman as a strategy consultant, advising Fortune 500 companies in M&A, organizational effectiveness, and growth strategy.

Grace earned her B.S. from the University of California, Berkeley, where she majored in Business Administration and minored in Public Policy. Outside of work, Grace enjoys Pilates, traveling, and following the latest in F1.

Erica Lockheimer is an operating advisor at Bessemer and the CEO & Founder of HumanizeHer, a platform dedicated to empowering women to thrive personally and professionally by redefining success on their own terms.

Erica brings over two decades of engineering and leadership experience in the technology sector. Most recently, she spent 13 years at LinkedIn, where she served as Vice President of Engineering. She led a range of high-impact teams including Growth, LinkedIn Learning (formerly known as Lynda.com), Glint, and LinkedIn’s Talent Solutions, playing a key role in scaling the company’s membership from 150 million to over one billion users. Earlier in her career, Erica held engineering roles at Good Technology, where she helped pioneer mobile enterprise solutions.

A longtime advocate for equity in tech, Erica founded LinkedIn’s Women in Tech (WIT) initiative, driving internal programs and external partnerships to support women in engineering globally. In recognition of her contributions, she was named one of the top 22 women engineers in the world by Business Insider in both 2014 and 2015.

Erica is a first-generation college graduate with a B.S. in Computer Engineering from San Jose State University, where she later delivered the 2018 commencement address. A Bay Area native and mother of two, she is passionate about building diverse teams, scaling early-stage initiatives, and fostering inclusive communities in tech.

Pedro Espinoza is an executive assistant for Bessemer’s IT department based out of the Larchmont office. Prior to joining Bessemer, Pedro was an administrative assistant at Bridgewater Associates. He also spent five years working with non-profit organizations in the arts and culture space.
Pedro holds a BFA in jazz guitar from the New School for Jazz and Contemporary Music. Pedro is passionate about health and wellness, sports, and jazz guitar.
Laura Dholakia is an operating advisor at Bessemer where she brings over twenty years of experience in technology, spanning strategy, analytics, and operational leadership.

As the vice president of business operations and analytics at LinkedIn, she led the company’s efforts to drive results through data, operational insights, and strategic initiatives. Her team was responsible for end-to-end strategy, performance management, and analytics across all across product, sales, marketing, customer support, and HR.

Prior to LinkedIn, Laura was an associate partner at McKinsey & Company where she focused on solving key strategic and operational issues for many of the world’s leading technology players over the course of more than thirty engagements. She started her career as a programmer at Trilogy Software, building online sales solutions for Fortune 500 clients before transitioning into various leadership roles within the company.
Laura graduated Phi Beta Kappa from Stanford University with dual degrees in mechanical engineering and English and earned her M.B.A. from Harvard Business School.
David Osborne is an operating advisor at Bessemer and a seasoned executive with over 30 years of enterprise technology sales and management experience.

Over his career, Dave has built and scaled inside, channel, and field sales organizations focused on software, services, and partnerships. In addition, Dave has been a general manager, overseeing North American and global P&Ls for both large and small companies.

Currently, Dave is the SVP of Alliances & Partnerships at Penguin Solutions, a division of SMART Global Holdings (SGH). Penguin Solutions is a computing company that designs and manages AI-optimized infrastructure. In his current role, Dave is responsible for identifying and managing go-to-market partnerships.

Most recently, Dave was the Executive Vice President of Channel Sales & Business Development at vCom Solutions, a privately held software and services company. In this role, he oversaw the development of vCom’s channel strategy, including the recruitment and management of new reseller partners.

Throughout his career, Dave has held management positions at Oracle, Kinecta, Comergent, and an exceptional 16-year journey at SAP-including a role as GM for SAP's global $500 million Customer Education & Training division. Additionally, in late 2019, he became the Chief Revenue Officer at PlanSource, and in 2021, he led a $200 million global sales organization at Skillsoft.
Dave holds a BS from the University of California, Berkeley, and resides in California.

Scott Ring is a partner, chief strategy officer, and general counsel based in the New York offices. He co-leads Bessemer’s global operations and is the head of legal and compliance activities, overseeing Bessemer’s fundraising strategy and management of investor relationships.

Scott manages Bessemer’s fundraising, fund structuring, liquidity, policy development and regulatory compliance functions, and many of the firm’s strategic initiatives. Scott also leads a team of professionals responsible for venture investment structuring, negotiation, and execution in the United States and abroad. His team partners with Bessemer's investment professionals to improve portfolio company performance, advising on transactions (including M&A), intellectual-property strategy, incentive compensation, and other strategic operational and transactional issues faced by Bessemer funded companies.

Previously, Scott was at the Silicon Valley legal advisory firm Venture Law Group and counseled entrepreneurs and venture capitalists on new venture formation, strategic alliances, investments, exits, board governance, and operational issues.
Scott holds a J.D. from Northwestern University School of Law, an M.B.A from Northwestern University’s Kellogg Graduate School of Management, and a B.A. in economics from the University of Michigan.

children.text: Sara Byrne is a partner and the Chief Financial Officer of Bessemer based on the east coast. As CFO Sara leads the team responsible for the financial operations of the firm. This includes investor reporting, tax compliance, tax structuring, management of the firm’s general partner entities and the firms global operating entities, fund formation, treasury and coinvestment program. Drawing on over two decades of experience, Sara is a technical anchor, and given her institutional knowledge, a mentor within the finance operations team contributing to investor communications, valuations, financial analysis, audit, and tax.
Previously, Sara worked at JP Morgan Partners. She is a graduate from Villanova University with a degree in accounting.
Justina Chung is a vice president in Bessemer’s London office, where she focuses on investments in SaaS, cloud infrastructure, consumer internet and marketplaces.

Before joining Bessemer, Justina was a vice president at SoftBank Vision Fund for software and marketplace investments in Europe, where she developed the fund’s HR Software roadmap and invested in companies such as Jobandtalent, Vestiaire Collective, Atom Learning, Trendyol, CMR Surgical, and Sorare. She also spent several years in the investment banking group of Goldman Sachs in London and Hong Kong, and in Credit Suisse in Hong Kong.
Outside of work, Justina enjoys skiing and reading biographies and dystopian science fiction novels.
She earned her bachelor's degree in economics from the University of Chicago and studied at the United World College in Hong Kong.

Spencer Ante is an operating advisor and communications and marketing executive with a history of building integrated global programs and leading multi-disciplinary teams for top companies that enhance corporate reputation and drive business results. He brings a background of strategic communications, digital innovation and editorial management experience from world-class organizations, including Meta and The Wall Street Journal. Spencer was named by Financial Narrative in 2024 as one of the top 50 of the most influential leaders in financial marketing and communications.

Most recently, he was Vice President of Public Affairs & Communications at American Express where led comms-marketing for its Technology Group. Prior to that, he was Head of Insights for Meta Foresight, where lead an editorial team responsible for thought leadership within the Brand Management Group of Meta's Global Business Marketing unit and helped reposition Meta as a leader in emerging technologies such as AI, AR and the metaverse.

Before joining Meta, Spencer held leadership roles at some of the world’s most influential PR and business advisory firms, including FTI Consulting, Weber Shandwick and Edelman. His work in journalism and marketing has received major recognition, including a Pulitzer Prize-nomination, Sigma Delta Chi Award for Public Service Journalism, National Magazine award, and Cannes Lions Titanium Grand Prix. Spencer is also the author of Creative Capital: Georges Doriot and the Birth of Venture Capital, published by Harvard Business Press.
Spencer lives in New Jersey with his wife, two children and rescue dog.
Bar Weiner is an investor in Bessemer’s New York City office, where he focuses on artificial intelligence, enterprise software applications, infrastructure and security.

Before joining Bessemer, Bar worked as an AI researcher and software engineer at Houzz and InfluxData, and later founded a generative AI procurement and RFP automation startup. He also held venture investing roles at Battery Ventures, the SoftBank Vision Fund and S32, and has been an active angel investor.

Bar graduated from Stanford University with both a bachelor’s and master’s degree in computer science, specializing in artificial intelligence. At Stanford, he led Cardinal Ventures, the university’s largest startup accelerator, and served as a teaching assistant for several courses at the Graduate School of Business and the School of Engineering.
Outside work, he enjoys hiking, snowboarding, surfing, spending time with his dog and trying new restaurants.
Irene Sheh is a senior executive assistant in Bessemer’s Silicon Valley office.

Irene earned a Bachelor of Science in marketing with a minor in ethnic studies from Santa Clara University. Before joining Bessemer, she was an executive assistant at NewView Capital, where she supported multiple partners, team events and office management. Irene also managed special events at Stanford University for high-profile donors and alumni, working in both the Development Office and the Graduate School of Education. Earlier in her career, she coordinated weddings and corporate functions as an event planner.
In her spare time, Irene enjoys reading thrillers, listening to pop culture podcasts and spending time with her family.
Dhruv Suri is portfolio monitoring solutions manager on Bessemer’s operations team based in India.
Prior to joining Bessemer, Dhruv worked at PwC India where he focused on valuations and strategy consulting. He also worked at Grant Thornton India focusing on valuations and assurance services.
Dhruv is a chartered accountant and earned his bachelor's degree from the University of Delhi. In his spare time, he enjoys running, traveling, and tennis.
Priya Kale is vice president of marketing for Bessemer’s India office in Bangalore.

Prior to joining Bessemer, Priya was at Elevation Capital for over four years where she spearheaded the rebranding and marketing functions of the fund. Priya began her career in regulatory affairs at Thomson Reuters in Singapore. She then went on to work for global anti-money laundering teams in Zurich and London at Credit Suisse before returning to India as a consultant with the Boston Consulting Group.

Priya earned her B.A. degree from St. Xavier's College, Mumbai with honors and an MSc. in International Political Economy from The London School of Economics. Outside of work, Priya is an avid reader of mythology, historical fiction, and world history, and loves to travel to the places she explores in books. She also is a meme collector who excels at making terrible puns.
Anurag is a vice president in the Bangalore office, where he focuses on consumer internet, fintech, health tech and SaaS.

Before joining Bessemer, Anurag was part of the investment team at Temasek, where he worked on growth and late-stage investments in consumer internet, retail, healthcare, and financial services. Prior to Temasek, he was a part of the investment team at Lighthouse Funds. He started his career as an investment banker at Alvarez & Marsal and Edelweiss Financial Services Limited.
Anurag earned a bachelor of commerce degree from Gujarat University and is a Chartered Accountant (rank holder). He is also an avid sports fan and enjoys playing basketball and cricket.

Blythe Yee is an operating advisor at Bessemer who brings over 20 years of experience in strategic communications at companies including LinkedIn, Intuit, and Sun Microsystems. Her expertise in leadership and organizational communications drives growth, performance, and trust-building in high-stakes situations. Blythe is passionate about intentional employee communications that foster thriving businesses and brands.

Currently Blythe is the Vice President of Employee Communications & Engagement at Freshworks Inc., (NASDAQ: FRSH), a customer engagement software for businesses of all sizes. In her role, she oversees communications, employee experience, and social impact initiatives for Freshworks' 5000 employee workforce worldwide.

Previously, Blythe was the Vice President of Employee Communications at LinkedIn (NYSE: LNKD) she led global communications across 30 offices and played a crucial role in scaling the organization from 8,000 to 20,000 employees. Blythe's background in HR and leadership development includes serving as chief of staff to the chief human resources officer at Sun Microsystems and working as a certified leadership coach. Prior to Sun, Blythe served as the director of corporate communications at Intuit, where she established the employee communications function and contributed to the company's recognition as a great place to work globally. Earlier in her career, she taught English in rural Japan and began her communications career in Tokyo, working on IBM's top customer program for the 1998 Winter Olympics in Nagano, Japan.

Apart from her professional engagements, Blythe has been an advisory board member of the University of Southern California Annenberg Center for Public Relations and continues to work with them in a consulting capacity. She holds an undergraduate degree in Economics and Japanese from the University of Michigan and a professional coaching certification from the Hudson Institute of Coaching. In her free time, she enjoys traveling, hiking, and volunteering.
Maneeta Shina is a senior executive assistant based out of Bessemer’s New York City office.
Maneeta has seven years of experience in the events industry. Prior to joining Bessemer, she was an executive assistant at Stone Harbor Investment Partners where she supported the HR and sales team.
Maneeta earned her BA in design management and innovation from De Montfort University. In her spare time, she enjoys traveling and spending time with her family, dog, and friends.

Anthony Lye is an operating advisor at Bessemer and the global head of the Apollo and the product-led growth business unit at Palantir Technologies (NYSE: PLTR), a software development company that specializes in big data analytics and known for their work with the US intelligence community, the U.S. Department of Defense, and several Fortune 500 companies.

Throughout his career, Anthony has been working on business and technology transformations, including distributed computing, early internet technologies, Software as a service (SaaS), Platform as a service (PaaS), and Infrastructure as a service (IaaS). Anthony has over 25 years of experience in the development of Customer Relationship Management (CRM), Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP), and Human Capital Management (HCM).

Prior to Palantir, Anthony served as the executive vice president and general manager of NetApp’s (NASDAQ: NTAP) public cloud business, where he led the growth from $500k to more than $500M in five and half years, including more than a dozen acquisitions. Before joining NetApp, Anthony held several leadership positions at cloud technology businesses, including HotSchedules, Siebel, Oracle, and Remedy leading fast-growth transformational businesses across product, engineering, sales, marketing, and customer success.

Anthony holds a Bachelor of Engineering degree from the University of Bath in England. He currently serves on the board of trustees at Bath University and is a senior advisor to the Boston Consulting Group and SUSE, an open-source software company that develops and sells Linux products to business customers. In addition, Anthony has established a scholarship for women in the School of Coding. Outside of work, Anthony enjoys spending time with his wife and their three children.

Lupe is an operating advisor at Bessemer and the vice president of sales at Oracle. Lupe brings over 20 years of experience working at the intersection of technology and automation to lead dynamic sales organizations across extended ecosystems and enable multi-million-dollar revenue growth.
Before joining Oracle in 2010, Lupe held executive positions for Fortune 500 and other corporations, including Eastman Kodak, Comergent, Informatica, Business Objects, SAP, and EMC.

Lupe earned his B.A. in Psychology from the University of California, Berkeley. Completed Accelerate Executive Insight (AEI) program for Oracle, in partnership with Michigan Ross School of Business and the University of Navarra IESE Business School in Barcelona, Spain, and Windsor, UK. Lupe lives in Northern California with his wife and two daughters.

Shannon Brayton is the Chief Marketing Officer and leads all the marketing and platform functions at Bessemer. She has more than 25 years of experience leading teams and shaping corporate narratives for some of the world’s most innovative and disruptive brands, most recently as Chief Marketing Officer of LinkedIn. She is currently a member of the Board of Directors of Quizlet and KQED. She is also an advisory board member at several companies and an active angel investor.

Shannon was named one of the world’s most influential CMOs for three consecutive years by Forbes Magazine, and she was described by PRWeek in 2017 as “a force of nature any company would want on their side.”

Shannon lives in the San Francisco Bay Area with her husband and two children. Her hobbies include reading the news, traveling with her family, and doing the New York Times crossword puzzle every day.

children.text: Cassio is an operating advisor at Bessemer and the chief information security officer at ServiceTitan, where he is responsible for establishing and maintaining the vision, strategy, and program to ensure information assets and technologies are adequately protected.

Prior to joining ServiceTitan in 2018, Cassio was the vice president of cyber resilience practice at Aon, a financial risk-mitigation Company, where he developed strategies and assessments to mitigate security risk. Cassio has held several information security positions at Fortune 500 companies and startups including NCR Corporation, Intuit, Symantec, and Cisco.

Cassio’s efforts in securing enterprises have been recognized by the information security community. He was the winner of the Information Security Leadership Awards for all Americas by (ISC)2, appointed one of the top 100 CISOs in the United States by his peers at CISO Connect, nominated one of the top CISOs in America by ISE, and a nominated for the web application security person of the year by OWASP.

Cassio earned his B.S. in computer science from Pontifícia Universidade Católica do Rio Grande do Sul in Brazil, an M.S. in software engineering from Santa Clara University, and an MBA in entrepreneurship and technology from the University of Southern California’s Marshall School of Business.
Laura Weisbord is a senior accounting associate based out of Bessemer’s Larchmont office.
Laura began her career at Ernst & Young where she primarily worked with financial services companies. Prior to joining Bessemer, she was on the tax team at Anchin, Anchin & Block.
Laura earned her MBA from SUNY New Paltz. In her spare time, she enjoys traveling, rugby, and running.

Paul Fifield is an operating advisor at Bessemer who brings extensive expertise as a four-time founder and early-stage company-building specialist. His passion lies in the highly creative early stages of a company's development.

After pioneering short-form, brand-funded entertainment in the early stages of the internet through his production company Guerrilla Productions,  Paul spotted the emerging B2B SaaS value creation opportunity and pivoted into technology.

Most recently in 2019,  Paul served as the CEO and co-founder of Sales Impact Academy, an ed-tech company offering an education and coaching platform for Go-to-Market teams. Under his leadership, the company experienced rapid growth during the pandemic, securing over $30M. Revenue grew to $1M after 12 months, then $5M a year later, and the business continues to thrive under a new CEO, with Paul moving to a board-only position in 2022.

Previously, Paul held the position of CRO at UNiDAYS, a digital identity startup in the student space. In just three years, he played a key role in elevating the company's revenue from $2M to $40M, with no external capital. Paul established and grew the Go-to-Market team from 2 to over 100 people, successfully expanding operations to New York and Sydney.

Paul's career highlights also include co-founding online design tool Ceros in New York in 2013,  raising a Series A and serving initially as CEO, before focusing on sales in the role of CRO.  In 2020 the business raised $100M from a notable venture capital firm and continues as an independent company with an exciting AI play that is anticipated to accelerate revenues past $100M.

Today Paul is actively involved in coaching CEOs of early-stage venture-backed businesses, serving on several boards, and developing a new venture called “In This Together”, a coaching platform and venture fund designed to support companies from Seed to Series A.  Apart from his professional engagements, Paul enjoys playing the guitar with his high-octane new indie punk band, studying Eastern philosophy and mindfulness, and incorporating cycling and running into his routine as he trains for an upcoming half Iron Man. He is a very proud father to his autistic teenage son and he currently resides in London, England.

Maha is a Vice President in Bessemer Venture Partners’ New York office, where she focuses on early-stage investments across the application-layer. She partners with founders building across B2B, consumer, and prosumer platforms, with a particular interest in how workflows are being reshaped in the LLM era across verticals.

Prior to Bessemer, Maha was an Associate Partner at Bain & Company, where she focused on growth strategy, operations, new business incubation, and private equity diligence across software, consumer, and healthcare.

Maha graduated cum laude from Dartmouth College with a BA in Economics. She holds an MBA with distinction from Harvard Business School and a Master in Public Policy from Harvard Kennedy School. Originally from Pakistan, she loves traveling, experimenting in the kitchen, and writing.

children.text: Yash Mehta is a senior portfolio monitoring associate at Bessemer Venture Partners and is a part of Bessemer’s remote operations team based in India, where he focuses on portfolio monitoring and valuations.
Prior to joining Bessemer, Yash worked as an articled assistant at an accounting firm focusing on transfer pricing and domestic tax.

Yash received his bachelor’s degree in commerce from Gujarat University. He has a CFA Level I certification and is currently pursuing Chartered Accountant qualification. In his spare time, he enjoys spending time with his dog, Arya, lifting weights, and supporting the football club Real Madrid.

Jessica Kleiman is an operating advisor at Bessemer and brings over 20 years of experience as a communications and public relations executive. Jessica loves to craft great stories that can help transform brands through powerful messaging and strategic marketing communications. She has deep experience across brand positioning, including corporate and internal communications, content development, public relations, and social media, particularly in the media, tech, design, and lifestyle sectors. She has worked for both early-stage tech startups and large, well-established organizations. Jessica has led communications for two IPOs and, over the course of her career, has worked with several founders to build their communications function from the ground up.

Most recently, Jessica was the senior vice president of global communications at Peloton, where she oversaw the brand’s public relations, corporate communications, internal communications, and social media initiatives. Before joining Peloton in 2018, she led consumer communications at Instagram. Prior to Instagram, Jessica spent 12 years at Hearst Magazines, where she drove PR efforts for 20 U.S. media brands including Cosmopolitan, Elle, Harper’s Bazaar, HGTV Magazine, and more. She started her career leading communications for The Knot (now the XO Group), where she spearheaded all marketing communications for the leading online wedding resource.
Jessica served on the Board of New York Women in Communications (NYWICI) for four years, first as VP-Strategic Planning and then as Chief Communications Officer. She co-authored the book,
Be Your Own Best Publicist: How to Use PR Techniques to Get Noticed, Hired, and Rewarded at Work
, and has written about branding and career issues for many national outlets.

Jessica earned a B.A. in communication from the University of Michigan. In her free time, she loves being at the beach, exercising, reading, cooking, and connecting with smart, talented people. She lives in Brooklyn, NY with her husband, daughter, and their Shih Tzu, Suzi.

Before Bessemer, Nikki built her career in design. She led event marketing at Frog Design, a global strategy and innovation consultancy specializing in creating transformative human experiences. She worked closely with Frog’s venture arm, Frog Ventures, supporting the portfolio companies’ marketing and PR strategies.
Both in and out of work, Nikki is a passionate planner and hostess.

Ross Biestman is chief revenue officer for ServiceTitan where he is responsible for the company’s sales, marketing, customer success, and revenue operations teams. He oversees the go-to-market strategy and execution of growth initiatives for ServiceTitan’s suite of software offerings.
Throughout his career working for software businesses in Silicon Valley, Ross has been a customer-centric executive charged with building high performing, revenue generating teams.

Prior to ServiceTitan, Ross served as vice president of sales at Lithium Technologies where he spearheaded revenue initiatives for four years, ultimately resulting in Lithium’s successful acquisition by Vista Equity Partners.

He’s held previous roles in software sales, mergers and acquisitions, and business development at companies such as Adobe, CrowdFlower, and Stealth HD (a business he co-founded that was acquired by Amazon).

Outside of work, Ross enjoys spending time with his wife, Rebecca, and two sons, Parker and Levi, at their home in Northern California. He serves on the board of the University of California Advisory Committee for Intercollegiate Athletics and is an advisor to an educational institute in Berkeley that provides scholarship and community building opportunities for college students. He loves to play golf, backcountry ski in the Sierra Nevada mountains, and always roots for the California Golden Bears.

Ross holds a Bachelor’s degree from the University of California, Berkeley, where he was an All-American on Cal’s Varsity Rugby team and won four consecutive collegiate national championships. He’s also earned a Master’s degree from the Said Business School at Oxford University.

Lara Cumberland is an operating advisor and a seasoned executive with more than 20 years of experience in M&A strategy, integration, and scaling operations for high-growth technology companies. She has led the evaluation, integration and value-creation of more than 200 acquisitions spanning AI, SaaS, payments, e-commerce, AR/VR, AdTech, hardware and security sectors.

Most recently, Lara served as Chief Operating Officer of Pacaso — the global prop-tech company focused on vacation home co-ownership — where she spearheaded cross-functional growth initiatives and global operationals. Prior to that, she was Vice President of M&A Integration & Strategic Initiatives at Meta Platforms (formerly Facebook), where she oversaw the integration of all global acquisitions for seven years and built out the company’s first team dedicated to executing strategic cross-company initiatives. Earlier in her career, Lara held senior M&A leadership roles at eBay / PayPal and IBM.

Lara partners with founders and leadership teams to drive value creation through disciplined M&A strategy, operational readiness for acquisition or exit, and repeatable scaled execution across functions. She brings the unique perspective of having served as both integrator (on the acquiring side) and operator (scaling business post-transaction).

Originally from Canada, she serves on the Board of The C100, a non-profit that champions Canadian technology entrepreneurs building global businesses. She splits her time between San Francisco and the Utah mountains where she enjoys powder skiing, live music, travel and time with her son.

Solmaz Shahalizadeh is an operating advisor at Bessemer, an executive and advisor in data and product, and a founding partner of Backbone Angels, a collective focused on funding more diverse and women-founded companies.

Most recently, she was the Vice President and Head of Data at Shopify, helping it grow from 100k to over 1.75 million merchants from 2013 to 2022. In her role, Solmaz was the voice of data in the senior leadership team and evangelized a culture of being data informed across the company. She spent her early years building the company’s financial data warehouse and analytics, and played a critical role in their successful IPO. With a passion to create experiences powered by data, she started and scaled Shopify’s portfolio of data products such as Shopify’s order fraud detection that runs in real-time on every order placed across Shopify platform, and Shopify Capital that has funded over 3B$ in cash advances to merchants based on machine learning models. As the leader of the data team and discipline, she grew Shopify’s data team to over 500 data scientists, engineers and product managers, and additionally took on leading the suite of merchant-facing analytical products to give Shopify merchants best-in-class analytical experiences.

Prior to Shopify, Solmaz worked as an analyst at Morgan Stanley and data scientist at McGill University, in the latter role she contributed to cancer research, using methods to build predictors of outcomes for breast cancer.

Solmaz is the winner of the Globe and Mail’s Report on Business Best Executive award in 2020, and a recipient of the Forty Under 40 by the Ottawa Business Journal in 2021, both recognizing her leadership and work in the Technology field.
Outside of advising companies, she has invested in and her love for technology in general, Solmaz likes to travel any chance she gets.
Mayank Verma is a portfolio monitoring associate on Bessemer’s India operations team.

Mayank holds a Bachelor of Commerce from Indira Gandhi National Open University and is a chartered accountant from the Institute of Chartered Accountants of India. Verma began his career during his articleship with Deloitte Pune in the statutory audit department. He later worked with Barclays Pune in their valuation control department and with Hira Infra Tek Limited, a UHNI family office, in the investment department.
Outside the office, Mayank enjoys watching football matches.

Talia Goldberg is a partner in Bessemer’s San Francisco office. She supports teams that leverage AI to create new categories and progress the way we live and work. She looks for founders building radically better products with unique distribution models, or those pushing the frontier.

Talia joined Bessemer in 2013. She is partner to Cognition, Discord, DeepL, fal AI, Fin (fka Intercom), Kindred, Mind Robotics, Papaya Global, Perplexity, Ramp, Recall, ServiceTitan, Shippo, Stubhub, Supermaven (now Cursor / XAI), and Toss, among others. Learn more on
her blog

. She was featured in

for Venture Capital.
Talia graduated from the University of Pennsylvania. She grew up in Portland, Oregon, which she insists is home to the best ice cream and pizza in America.

qAndA.answer: Bessemer invested me for over a decade via an apprenticeship model, let me make mistakes, figure out my own authentic style to working with founders and investing, and gave me the autonomy to push into new areas and pursue ideas and teams when it was uncomfortable, controversial, and/or not yet obvious.
qAndA.question: What Bessemer gave you that you couldn't have found anywhere else is...

qAndA.answer: Poor Charlie's Almanack. First, Charlie Munger is hilarious. Second, he outlines many of the natural human tendencies that lead to misjudgments and error. Why smart people make bad decisions. Recognizing the behaviors and obsessing over incentives is step one to making better decisions. Three, it offers great mental models that apply just as well to investing and company building as it does to every day life.

For seven consecutive years, Ray participated in the World Economic Forum Annual Meetings in Davos, Switzerland. During his tenure, he served as a member of the World Economic Forum’s Global Agenda Council on Space Security.

. He has a strong interest in fintech infrastructure, embedded financial services, and the entrepreneurs that are solving the hardest problems facing both consumers and businesses in our current financial system.

During the company’s growth phase, Charles became the director of mobile and international business development and built strategic partnerships with media companies, carriers, and OEMs in key growth markets.
Prior to Foursquare, Charles spent six years in investment banking and equity capital markets focusing on the technology, media, and telecom sectors.

He earned his MBA from the Wharton School, Master of Arts in international studies from the Lauder Institute at the University of Pennsylvania, and a Bachelor of Arts in history from Northwestern University.

qAndA.answer: Integrity. Entrepreneurship requires a little bit of insanity. To take the leap, to get others to join you, to get customers to believe in you, all before it's real, takes a complex mix of traits to make it all happen. The founders I admire the most are the ones who can get through all the selling, the building, the highs and lows with integrity. Caring deeply about their team, their customers, their shareholders and keeping the long game always top of mind.

qAndA.question: If not this, then...

qAndA.answer: Melio. We made an entirely team-based investment at the seed stage, the company changed ideas, approaches, and even the company name several times in the early days, but the Melio journey taught me how rewarding it can be when we trust our instinct to back world-class entrepreneurs and support them on their ambitious journey without being didactic and forcing them down certain paths.
qAndA.question: The investment that changed how you think was...

qAndA.answer: I collapsed from heat exhaustion and dehydration once during mile 23 of the Chicago Marathon on a historically hot and humid day. There are positives that stem from being a type A, somewhat crazily determined person, but not respecting my limitations that day in the face of unusual conditions outside of my control to the point of failure was a painful lesson. Since, I more often adjust to my surroundings and don't always trying to plow through no matter what.
qAndA.question: The failure that taught you the most was...

qAndA.answer: Grit, intellectual honesty, and the ability to hire people smarter than you.

qAndA.answer: Letting down the entrepreneurs who choose to work with me. I don't think I've ever invested in a business that didn't have other options on which VC to work with. I make promises when I partner with entrepreneurs and my biggest fear is not living up to them.

Vikram earned his Bachelor of Commerce from Osmania University and is a qualified Chartered Accountant. Outside of work, Vikram is passionate about cricket as it helps him stay focused and motivated.

Sandy Grippo is a partner and chief operating officer in the New York office. She works closely with Bessemer’s global team and represents the firm with financial partners, institutions, and investors. In addition, she oversees all financial operations of the firm and its investment funds including valuations, accounting, budgeting, financial systems, audits, reporting, treasury, tax planning, and compliance as well as policy development. She also leads the human resources and information technology teams at Bessemer.

As a co-lead for the day-to-day global operations, Sandy chairs the weekly investment meetings, manages fund structuring, ensures proper policies and controls are followed, and executes on strategic initiatives.

Sandy joined Bessemer in 2002 bringing almost a decade of experience in accounting and financial reporting for private investment funds. At J.P. Morgan Partners, she was a vice president where she developed expertise in partnership accounting, partnership taxes, and fund operations. Her responsibilities included financial management for the $5.4 billion J.P. Morgan Partners Global Investors fund.

After graduating with a degree in accounting from Lehigh University and earning her CPA, Sandy began her career at Ernst and Young where she spent five years specializing in hedge fund and private equity clients.

Doug Robinson is an operating advisor at Bessemer and a seasoned enterprise software executive with over 30 years of experience spanning ERP, HCM, SCM, and CRM. Doug currently serves on the Board of Directors at Varicent and on the Advisory Board of Ema AI.

Most recently, Doug capped a 15-year career at Workday, having joined at $25M in annual revenue and retiring at $8.9B, as Company Co-President, where he was responsible for overseeing Workday's go-to-market efforts across the globe and all industries, and for driving continued revenue growth in new and emerging markets. Prior to the Co-President role, Doug served as executive vice president of global sales and solution consulting, and held a variety of leadership roles at the company focused on both medium and large enterprise customer segments, as well as leading the education & government business and sales & operations strategy. Most recently, Kellie was the Chief Customer Officer at Gainsight where she was responsible for leading all post-sales functions which includes a team of 400+ globally across customer success management, account management, support, professional services, digital and scaled programs, and CS operations. She spent nearly 8 years at Gainsight helping to scale and grow the CS organization and company from ~$40M to $200+M in revenue. During her tenure, she worked with thousands of CS professionals and customers to help advise and coach them on their CS strategy.

Kellie has recently become a published author of the book “Digital Customer Success: Why the next frontier of CS is digital and how you can leverage it to drive durable growth.” She believes that the next frontier of customer success will leverage intelligent and personalized digital experiences to create a more effective customer experience while driving increased productivity for the business.

Prior to Gainsight, Kellie has spent her career in customer-facing roles spanning across sales, account management and customer success, with a background in HCM at ADP. She has found her forever home in customer success at the intersection of what she is energized by most - forging prosperous customer relationships through value realization and cultivating professional growth for teammates.
Kellie lives in Austin, TX where she is a proud wife and mother to two daughters, Brynn (12) and Brooklyn (10). She also deeply loves her three mini bernedoodle “fur babies”, Ollie, Colton and Myla.
